qs.q: Why did Arthur throw the brick at the Junk Man?
a: He was playing a game with friends.
He was angry about a school test.
He saw the old man wearing his dead father's cap and lost control.
qs.e: Grief turned into anger in one terrible moment.

qs.q: 'Reluctantly, he turned back toward the garage.' What does reluctantly mean?
a: Not wanting to, but doing it anyway
qs.e: Slow feet, but he kept going.

qs.q: What did Mr. Hampton ask the judge to do instead of sending Arthur to juvie?
a: Let Arthur go with no punishment
Make Arthur work for him until his arm healed
Make Arthur pay a big fine
qs.e: He wanted a second chance, not payback.

qs.q: Someone called the Junk Man a 'worthless' trash picker. What does the ending -less mean in worthless?
qs.e: Worthless means without any worth.

qs.q: What were Mom's new rules mainly meant to do?
a: Keep Arthur out of trouble and help him share his feelings
qs.e: Mom wanted her son safe and talking.

qs.q: Officer Billie said, 'I don't care ___ you get lost, sick or tired.' Which word fits: weather or whether?
qs.e: Whether means 'if'. Weather is rain or snow.

qs.q: What was the main message of Officer Billie's first meeting with Arthur?
a: He should find a new job.
He was free to do as he liked.
He had a second chance and must not mess it up.
qs.e: Strict words, but a real second chance.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton misspelled Arthur's name. What does the beginning mis- mean?
qs.e: Mis- means wrongly, so misspelled means spelled wrong.

qs.q: What was Arthur's job each Saturday for Mr. Hampton?
a: Collecting things from a list called the Seven Most Important Things
Washing the cart and sweeping the garage
qs.e: A strange list with a secret purpose.

qs.q: Which sentence best sums up chapters One to Twelve?
a: A judge becomes friends with a tattoo artist.
A family moves to a new city.
A boy wins a prize at school.
A boy who hurt an old man must work for him and starts to wonder about a mysterious list.
qs.e: The mystery begins with one brick.

qs.q: Arthur's anger was really tangled up with missing his dad. What helps when a feeling is too big?
qs.e: Big anger is often sadness in a costume!

qs.q: Mr. Hampton chose a second chance over revenge. What does that show?
a: Old people are easy to fool
qs.e: A second chance can be the strongest gift.

qs.q: Arthur never knew the Junk Man had a real name. What can we learn?
a: Everyone has a name and a story
qs.e: Everybody is somebody, even before we meet them!

qs.q: Arthur snapped at little Barbara when she asked scary questions. What would be kinder?
a: Answer gently, because she is scared too
qs.e: Little hearts hurt too, so go gently.

qs.q: Officer Billie told Arthur 'no excuses.' What is the lesson?
a: Own your choices and show up
qs.e: Own it, then fix it. That's brave.

qs.q: Arthur used different things than the list asked for because it was 'close enough.' What can we learn?
a: Do what was asked, or ask why
qs.e: Almost right is still not right!

qs.q: Arthur lied to Groovy Jim and felt guilty. Why does honesty feel better?
qs.e: Truth is light; lies are backpacks full of rocks.

qs.q: Arthur's mom made a rule: talk to her when you're upset. Why does this help?
a: Sharing a feeling makes it lighter
qs.e: A worry shared is a worry halved!

qs.q: Arthur wanted to quit the cart job, but he went back. What does this show?
a: Hard jobs are never worth it
qs.e: Brave means trying even when it's tough.

qs.q: Arthur's bad cart wheel kept sticking, but he kept trying to fix it. What does that teach?
a: Keep trying small fixes, step by step
Give the cart to someone else
qs.e: Stuck wheels move with patience and a good kick!

qs.q: How did Arthur feel at school after he came back from juvie?
a: Popular, because everyone wanted to hear his story
Happy to be with old friends
qs.e: An invisible box around him.

qs.q: 'The garage was deserted.' What does deserted mean?
qs.e: Deserted places echo.

qs.q: Why was Arthur dreading putting up the Christmas tree?
a: He was too busy with school.
Mom told him it was too hard.
His dad always did it, and he missed him.
He had never seen a tree before.
qs.e: The tree reminded him of Dad.

qs.q: Mom's bills were 'unopened.' What does un- mean in unopened?
qs.e: Un- plus opened means not opened.

qs.q: What did Arthur discover was the first important thing?
a: Lights, which brought hope and togetherness back to his family
qs.e: Little lights, big hope.

qs.q: Mom gave Arthur six silver 'peace' dollars, and Mr. Hampton's work was a 'masterpiece.' Which is right?
a: Peace means a part; piece means calm.
Peace means calm; piece means a part or a work.
qs.e: Peace is calm. Piece is a bit of something.

qs.q: What did Arthur learn about Officer Billie at Christmas?
a: She wanted him back in juvie.
She has a kind side beneath her tough manner.
She had stopped caring about him.
qs.e: Caramel corn from a no-nonsense cop!

qs.q: Arthur 'dreaded' putting up the tree. How is dread different from regret?
a: Dread is about the past; regret is about the future.
Dread is happy; regret is angry.
Dread and regret mean exactly the same.
Dread is fear of what's coming; regret is sorrow about what's done.
qs.e: Dread looks forward. Regret looks back.

qs.q: What did Arthur realize about the things people throw away?
a: They can matter to someone else for reasons you may not see.
qs.e: Some trash is hidden treasure.

qs.q: Why did Arthur rush to help Squeak at school?
a: He was looking for a fight.
He couldn't stand seeing someone treated cruelly.
qs.e: Arthur knew how it felt to be punished.

qs.q: Arthur gave excuses, but Officer Billie wanted a straight answer. What is the lesson?
a: Listen to the question and answer it honestly
qs.e: Straight answers beat long excuses.

qs.q: At school, everyone avoided Arthur because of his past. What should we remember?
a: People are only their worst moment
qs.e: One mistake isn't the whole story!

qs.q: Groovy Jim said 'vision' means looking deeper to see possibilities. How could you use that?
a: Look at what something could become
Only trust what you see first
qs.e: Look twice, see the sparkle in the junk!

qs.q: Arthur's family laughed over the fallen tree even though they were sad. What does that show?
a: Laughing is rude when you're sad
It's okay to laugh in hard times
qs.e: Laughter makes heavy hearts a little lighter.

qs.q: The tree lights made the family feel hopeful. What do small bright things teach us?
a: Little lights can warm a dark time
qs.e: One little light can brighten a whole room!

qs.q: Someone threw out a flowerpot, but it became the perfect gift. What can we learn?
a: Things can matter more to someone else
qs.e: One person's junk is another's treasure!

qs.q: Mom threw out Dad's cap, thinking it did not matter, but it mattered to Arthur. What helps?
qs.e: Asking beats guessing, every time.

qs.q: Barbara learned a lot from Mr. Hampton just by being friendly and curious. What does that show?
qs.e: A friendly hello can unlock great stories!

qs.q: Arthur helped Squeak even though nobody asked him to. What does that show?
qs.e: Real heroes help even when they're scared.

qs.q: Officer Billie seemed grumpy, yet she shared her caramel corn. What do we learn?
qs.e: Under a tough shell can be a soft heart!

quizzes.label: The Second Important Thing to Thirty-Four

qs.q: Why did Squeak keep sitting with Arthur?
a: He wanted to copy Arthur's homework.
He wanted a friend and wanted to thank Arthur for the rescue.
qs.e: A friendship started with a lunch bag.

qs.q: Arthur saw 'a wall of shimmering gold and silver.' What does shimmering mean?
a: Shining with a soft, flickering light
qs.e: Like sunlight on a pond.

qs.q: What secret did Arthur discover inside Mr. Hampton's garage?
a: A huge sculpture of heaven built from trash
qs.e: Trash turned into a shimmering heaven.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton looked 'exhausted.' What does exhausted mean?
qs.e: Out of energy, like a drained battery.

qs.q: What did Mr. Hampton mean by the Seven Most Important Things?
a: They were gifts for the judge.
They were rules for good behavior.
They were the building blocks of heaven.
qs.e: The list had a purpose all along.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton called the sculpture his 'masterpiece.' Masterpiece is master + piece. What does it mean?
a: A piece of a master key
A work made with great skill
qs.e: A piece made by a master. Simple and grand.

qs.q: Why did Arthur say he could not keep working for Mr. Hampton?
a: He was tired of the cart.
Mr. Hampton was dying, and it reminded Arthur of his dad's death.
qs.e: Too much loss, too close.

qs.q: Arthur wondered if 'throne' was a mistake for 'thrown-out.' What is the difference?
a: A throne is a royal chair; thrown is the past of throw.
Throne is a verb; thrown is a chair.
Thrown is a king's chair; throne means tossed.
qs.e: Same sound, different spelling and meaning!

qs.q: How did Squeak stand up for Arthur in the cafeteria?
a: He stood on a table with a sign inviting the bullies to throw things at him.
qs.e: A tiny hero with a big sign.

qs.q: What helped Arthur decide to keep going with the project?
a: Squeak's advice that he shouldn't give up on Mr. Hampton
qs.e: A friend can steady a shaky heart.

qs.q: Squeak sat with Arthur even though everyone else stayed away. What does that show?
a: Friendship starts with a kind choice
Lonely kids should be left alone
qs.e: One seat can start a big friendship.

qs.q: Squeak happily shared his foil without asking for anything back. What can we learn?
qs.e: Sharing a little can mean a lot.

qs.q: After hearing Mr. Hampton was sick, Arthur wanted to run away from it all. What helps most?
a: Talk to a friend you trust
qs.e: A friend can carry part of the heavy bag.

qs.q: Squeak said, 'You helped me last time. This time, it was my turn.' What does a good friend do?
qs.e: Friends take turns being the hero.

qs.q: Squeak stood on the table, even though he looked silly. What does that show?
a: Standing up for friends takes courage
qs.e: Courage looks different than muscles.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton said the brick that hurt him actually 'saved' him. What does this show?
a: How we see something can change its meaning
qs.e: The same story can have a brighter ending.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton said building heaven takes years and a lifetime. What does this teach?
a: Beautiful things take time and patience
qs.e: Great things grow one tiny piece at a time.

qs.q: The nurse offered Arthur juice and cookies, and he said no, though he was hungry. What would be wiser?
a: Accept help when you need it
qs.e: Saying yes to help is okay.

qs.q: Officer Billie told Arthur the hard truth plainly. Why is honesty important, even when it hurts?
a: Because it lets you prepare and trust
qs.e: Truth is a hard hug, but it's still a hug.

qs.q: Arthur kept having bad dreams about his dad. What does this tell us?
a: Missing someone shows how much we love them
You should stop thinking about people
qs.e: Missing someone is love with nowhere to go.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Hampton begin building heaven?
a: He wanted to sell his art.
After the war, he dreamed of making something beautiful from broken things.
qs.e: Death and War became something beautiful.

qs.q: The little box 'looked fragile.' What does fragile mean?
qs.e: Handle with care, like eggs.

qs.q: Why was Arthur upset when he learned his mom had a boyfriend?
a: He felt Roger was replacing his dad.
qs.e: Hearts are loyal, even when it's complicated.

qs.q: Soda bottles on a tree were a family 'tradition.' What is a tradition?
a: Something a family does the same way year after year
qs.e: Same fun thing, every spring.

qs.q: How did Arthur's opinion of Roger slowly change?
a: He saw that Roger was kind, honest and good at fixing things.
qs.e: Fair chances sometimes turn into friends.

qs.q: Lightbulb is a compound word (light + bulb). Which word is also a compound word?
qs.e: Bird plus house makes birdhouse.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Hampton ask Arthur so much about his dad?
a: He cared about the good things in his dad's life.
He wanted to write a book.
qs.e: Someone finally asked about his dad's life.

qs.q: Arthur hated using words like 'passed away.' Which sentence uses passed and past correctly?
a: Grandpa past away in the past year.
Grandpa passed away in the passed year.
Grandpa past away in the passed year.
Grandpa passed away in the past year.
qs.e: Passed is an action. Past means before now.

qs.q: What was the point of the soda bottle tradition?
a: To pour out things you're not proud of and feel lighter
qs.e: Out with the guilt, in with the spring.

qs.q: What problem faced Arthur after Mr. Hampton died?
a: The landlord would clear out the garage unless the rent was paid.
qs.e: A race to save heaven in a garage.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton turned broken things from war into something beautiful. What can we learn?
a: Something good can grow out of hard times
qs.e: Even cracks can let the light in.

qs.q: Smashing the mirrors made Arthur feel free of his worries. What does this show?
a: Letting go of worry can feel light
qs.e: Let go of the weight, feel the lift!

qs.q: Arthur disliked Roger before even meeting him. Then he liked parts of him. What is the lesson?
a: Give people a fair chance before deciding
qs.e: Wait to meet the person before you judge.

qs.q: At supper with Roger, Arthur felt he was letting his dad down. What is true?
a: You must hate new people to love someone you lost
You can love someone and still welcome new good people
qs.e: Hearts have plenty of room.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton asked about Arthur's dad's life, not his death. Why is that kind?
a: It makes people remember the happy parts
qs.e: Remember how they lived, not just how they left.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton said, 'Anything of value takes time.' What does this teach?
a: Good things need patience and care
qs.e: Slow and sparkly wins the day.

qs.q: Putting the bottle on the tree was a way to let go of guilt. What could you do after a mistake?
a: Say sorry, learn, and forgive yourself
qs.e: Pour it out, then plant something new.

qs.q: Mr. Hampton said, 'Don't wait for a better time.' What does this mean for us?
a: Start working on your dreams now
qs.e: Today is the best time to begin.

qs.q: Arthur smashed the mirrors while careful Squeak wrapped the bulbs. What does this show?
a: Everyone has different strengths that help a team
Teams should be all the same
qs.e: A team works best with different superpowers.

qs.q: Groovy Jim gave all his money and promised to keep watch. What kind of friend is he?
a: One who helps and keeps his promises
qs.e: Real friends show up, even when it costs.

qs.q: How did Arthur and Squeak try to raise money for the garage?
a: They put decorated coffee cans in shops around town.
They asked the judge for a loan.
qs.e: Coffee cans do the heavy lifting.

qs.q: The cans said 'Donate.' What does donate mean?
a: Give money or things to help
qs.e: Donate means to give to help.

qs.q: What brought the most attention to Mr. Hampton's work?
a: A newspaper article after a reporter visited the garage
A phone call to the mayor
qs.e: One card in one can opened a big door.

qs.q: Squeak suggested 'Save a Unique Work of Art.' Which word starts with uni- meaning 'one,' like unique?
qs.e: One wheel, one of a kind.

qs.q: What did the art museum decide to do with the Throne?
a: Put it on display next week
Keep it in its storage collection until it had room
Give it back to the landlord
qs.e: Saved, even if it had to wait.

qs.q: Someone said heaven should 'reflect' the people looking at it. What does reflect mean?
qs.e: Mirrors and foil both reflect.

qs.q: What did Arthur realize about the Seven Most Important Things?
a: They were a joke by the judge.
They were also the building blocks of his own redemption.
They were a list of chores.
qs.e: The list was building him, too.

qs.q: The museum people would talk it over with 'the board.' Which sentence uses board and bored correctly?
a: The bored met, but I was board.
The bored met, but I was bored.
The board met, but I was bored.
The board met, but I was board.
qs.e: A board decides; bored means not interested.

qs.q: How does the story end, seven years later?
a: The Throne is shown in a museum, and people keep coming to see it.
qs.e: The people kept coming, just as he said.

qs.q: What surprising connection did Squeak reveal about his dad?
a: His dad was a museum director.
His dad was the delivery driver who found Mr. Hampton after the brick.
qs.e: A big circle of kindness and luck.

qs.q: Arthur's mom said, 'Sometimes in life you have to let things go.' What does this mean?
a: Starting over isn't the same as forgetting
qs.e: Letting go makes room for new good things.

qs.q: Arthur said something hurtful to his mom, then apologized. What is the lesson?
a: Words can hurt, so say sorry honestly
qs.e: A real sorry is a bandage for the heart.

qs.q: Squeak tried many different words on the coffee cans, and one worked. What can we learn?
a: Try several ways until one works
qs.e: Keep trying, a winner is in there!

qs.q: Arthur and Squeak both weren't who people thought they were. What does this show?
a: Labels don't tell the whole story about a person
qs.e: People are bigger than their labels.

qs.q: Squeak's dad saved Mr. Hampton, who saved Arthur, who saved Squeak. What does this show?
a: Kindness passes from person to person
Saving others is a job for adults
qs.e: One kind act can start a happy chain!

qs.q: Arthur and Squeak asked to keep their names out of the newspaper article. What does this show?
qs.e: Real helpers don't need a spotlight.

qs.q: The museum visitors guessed wrong and called the foil balls Ping-Pong balls. What should Arthur do?
a: Politely speak up about what he knows
qs.e: If you know the story, share it kindly.

qs.q: At his birthday game, Arthur had fun but felt sad his dad was missing. What does that show?
a: You can feel happy and sad at the same time
Only one feeling at a time is okay
Fun is wrong when you're sad
qs.e: Hearts can hold two feelings at once.

qs.q: The Throne went to storage, not display. Officer Billie said, 'Nothing in this world is perfect.' What is the lesson?
a: Be thankful for good results while hoping for more
qs.e: A good ending can still be a bit bumpy.

qs.q: Years later, the boy who threw a brick helped open a museum exhibit. What does this show?
qs.e: Your worst day is not your whole story!
